solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: If clue initially reads badly, strike it! (7)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is an instruction about the answer: a lucifer is the thing you strike.

indicatorNotes.initially: 'initially' means at the start, so only the first letter of 'reads' is taken
indicatorNotes.badly: letters that read badly are out of order, so they must be rearranged

annotation.surface: An exasperated solver, fed up with a garbled clue, wants to strike it out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strike it!' looks like crossing out the clue, but it points at a match you strike. A lucifer is an old word for a friction match.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: the old friction match called a lucifer is lit by striking it, so the command names what you do to it.

entries.clue: Bet core part of livelihood’s to be superseded by ChatGPT, etc (4)

indicatorNotes.to be superseded by: to supersede is to take the place of, so AI replaces the core of the word

blocks.note: LIVELIHOOD loses its core IVELIHOO, leaving L at the front
ChatGPT and its kind are AI, artificial intelligence
the final letter of LIVELIHOOD, left after the core goes

annotation.surface: A worried worker predicts that AI chatbots will take over the heart of their job.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a real fear about AI taking jobs, and literally AI takes the core of LIVELIHOOD. 'Bet' is a past tense: you laid a fiver on a horse.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are past tenses of wagering: to lay money on a horse is to bet it.

entries.clue: Accountant cycling in retirement, huffs and puffs [and] rests (7)

indicatorNotes.in retirement: retiring means drawing back, so the word is written backwards
indicatorNotes.cycling: a cycle goes round, so a letter from one end travels round to the other

blocks.note: PANTS (breathes hard), turned round to STNAP, then its S cycled to the end

annotation.surface: A retired accountant takes up cycling and finds himself wheezing, so stops for breathers.
annotation.walkthrough: The picture of an out-of-breath pensioner on a bike hides two moves on one word: turn it round, then rotate a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the plural verb sense: to catnap is to doze briefly, which is a way of resting.

entries.clue: It’s strange if one daughter’s not had drink after sacrifice in God’s name (3,8,4)

indicatorNotes.not: 'one daughter's not' says one D is not there, so it is dropped
indicatorNotes.after: 'after' sets the preceding letters behind FORGO in the answer

blocks.note: to forgo is to give up

blocks.clueFragment: It’s strange if one daughter’s not
blocks.note: ODDNESS (the fact of being strange) with one D for daughter removed

annotation.surface: Someone thinks it odd that one daughter has not had a drink after the religious offering.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It’s strange' stands for ODDNESS, and losing one of its two Ds leaves one. The order is FORGO first, then the rest, which 'had' the drink after it.
annotation.definitionFit: Equivalent exclamations of exasperation, one invoking goodness and the other God.

entries.clue: It can be difficult to find equal treatment with power ceded to queen (6)

annotation.definition: It can be difficult to find

indicatorNotes.ceded to: to cede is to hand over, so P hands its place over to R

blocks.note: R = Regina, queen; it takes the place of P
PARITY (equality) with its P, power, taken out

annotation.surface: A complaint that fair treatment is hard to come by when power passes to the monarch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It can be difficult to find' is a whole-phrase definition dressed as a comment on equality.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: something scarce, by its nature, takes effort to track down.

entries.clue: Hydrogen injected into carbon, mainly to support frame (7)

indicatorNotes.injected into: an injection goes inside, so H is put inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.mainly: 'mainly' means for the most part, so ASSIST keeps all but its last letter

blocks.note: C is the symbol for carbon
H is the symbol for hydrogen

annotation.surface: A chemistry note: hydrogen is added to carbon, largely to strengthen a molecular framework.
annotation.walkthrough: The chemistry surface makes 'frame' look like a molecular lattice; it is the base of a car.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the load-bearing framework of a vehicle, on which the body is mounted.

entries.clue: Peach [or] prune that is seen peeled (5-3)

indicatorNotes.peeled: peeling takes off the skin, so the outer letters come off

blocks.note: SPIED (seen) with its first and last letters removed

annotation.surface: Two fruits, a peach and a prune, with something noticed about one being peeled.
annotation.walkthrough: The fruit-bowl surface puts 'Peach' and 'prune' side by side, but here 'Peach' is a person and 'prune' is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal terms of endearment: calling someone a peach means they are lovely, as does the answer.

entries.clue: Bit of a hoo-ha derailed precautions at llama farm ultimately (1,5,2,1,6)

indicatorNotes.derailed: a derailed train leaves its tracks in disorder, so the letters are jumbled
indicatorNotes.ultimately: 'ultimately' means in the end, so the last letters of llama and farm are taken

blocks.note: the last letters of llamA and farM

annotation.surface: A fuss at a llama farm when safety measures went wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes the fuss real; the answer says the fuss was over nothing much.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a great commotion over a trivial matter, which is what a hoo-ha usually amounts to.

entries.clue: Dreadful opening piece from Italian serial composer (7)

indicatorNotes.Dreadful: a dreadful arrangement is a bad one, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.opening piece from: the opening piece of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A critic pans the opening of an Italian twelve-tone composer's work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Serial composer' suggests twelve-tone music, but 'serial' is only fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Antonio Salieri, Mozart's Italian contemporary and supposed rival, wrote operas.

entries.clue: Wear this running in street? (10)

indicatorNotes.running: letters left running about are out of order, so they are rearranged
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' puts the jumble inside the abbreviation for street

blocks.note: ST = street, the abbreviation, which goes round the jumble

annotation.surface: Advice on what to put on for a jog along the road.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: read straight, it recommends the answer as running gear.
annotation.definitionFit: &lit: read straight, the clue describes a loose cotton top, the kind of thing worn for a run down the road.

entries.clue: Try to make sense of painter prettifying houses (9)

indicatorNotes.houses: to house is to hold inside, so the words before it contain the answer

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap, after pa- and before -tifying

annotation.surface: An artist making houses look prettier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Houses' looks like the painter's subject; it is the instruction that the two words contain the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to construe or explain the meaning of something.

entries.clue: Bit of Scrabble on Boxing Day, Mark? (5)

indicatorNotes.Boxing: to box something is to enclose it, so TILE encloses D

annotation.surface: Someone asks Mark whether he played Scrabble on Boxing Day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boxing Day' reads as the holiday after Christmas, but 'Boxing' is the container and 'Day' is just D. 'Mark' looks like a name.
annotation.definitionFit: Hypernym: a squiggle written over a letter, as in Spanish ñ, is one kind of diacritical mark.

entries.clue: Feeding spirit, shattered tenor had kip, missing intro to national anthem (5,3,6)

indicatorNotes.Feeding: food goes inside, so the anagram is fed into ZEST
indicatorNotes.shattered: something shattered is in pieces, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
indicatorNotes.missing: 'missing' means lacking, so N is left out

blocks.clueFragment: tenor had kip, missing intro to national
blocks.note: TENOR HAD KIP without N (first letter of national), then jumbled

annotation.surface: An exhausted tenor snoozes and misses the start of the national anthem.
annotation.walkthrough: The singer in the surface fits the answer: Handel's anthem has been sung at every British coronation since 1727.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Handel's coronation anthem of 1727, named after the priest who anointed Solomon.

entries.clue: Wet blankets outside during short run (10)

indicatorNotes.outside: 'outside' puts the first word around the second

blocks.note: a misery is a gloomy killjoy

annotation.surface: Damp bedding is left out while a brief spell passes.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'wet blanket' and a 'misery' are both people who spoil the fun. 'Short run' is television, not athletics.
annotation.definitionFit: Television sense of run: a drama shown over a small number of episodes has only a brief run.

entries.clue: What’s here: villains ideally? (6)

indicatorNotes.What’s here: 'what's here' asks what is contained in the words that follow, so the answer is held within them

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap, after vill- and before -ally

annotation.surface: A caption pointing at the place where criminals ought to be.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer describes itself: it sits in the middle of 'villains ideally', and ideally villains are in prison, which is the slang sense.
annotation.definitionFit: &lit: slang for serving a prison sentence, where villains ideally are, and also where the answer sits in the phrase.

entries.clue: Sign me up to gain access to beauty contract (8)

indicatorNotes.to gain access to: gaining access means getting in, so I'M IN goes inside DISH

blocks.note: a dish is an attractive person
'I'm in!' is what you say to join something

annotation.surface: A would-be model asks to be signed so she can get a beauty contract.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun going with 'beauty', but it is the verb: shrink.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, verb sense: to become smaller or shrink.

entries.clue: Continue unchanging message, penning discrimination [and] slurs (8)

indicatorNotes.penning: to pen is to shut in an enclosure, so the message encloses the next piece

blocks.note: to be is to remain as you are, as in 'let it be'
an SMS is a text message
an ear for music is discrimination between sounds

annotation.surface: A repeated message containing prejudice, and abusive remarks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Discrimination' sounds like prejudice, which suits 'slurs', but here it is a fine ear for sound.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative synonym, verb sense: to smear or sully someone's reputation.

entries.clue: I note response to where duke[’s] suffering embarrassment (2,3,3)

annotation.surface: Someone writes that the duke is embarrassed about where he is.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Embarrassment' here is the old sense of financial difficulty, as in pecuniary embarrassment.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom from red ink in accounts: being overdrawn, which is the dated money sense of embarrassment.

entries.clue: Lacy kit’s modelled in such a way? (7)

annotation.definition: Lacy kit’s modelled in such a way?

indicatorNotes.modelled: to model is to shape, so the letters are shaped into a new order

annotation.surface: A catwalk critic suggests the lace outfit was worn in poor taste.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the adverb describes how lacy kit might well be modelled.
annotation.definitionFit: &lit: read straight, the clue asks for a manner of modelling lingerie, and cheap, tasteless is the manner meant.

entries.clue: Starting to gag’s consistent with smoke (6)

indicatorNotes.Starting to: the start of a word is its first letter, so gag gives G

blocks.note: as per = in keeping with, consistent with

annotation.surface: Choking is what you'd expect from breathing smoke.
annotation.walkthrough: The gagging surface fits: a cheap cigarette makes you gasp.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang: an old word for a cheap cigarette, and a cigarette is a smoke.

entries.clue: Vivid description [of] old Northerner having curries regularly (7)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so every other letter of curries is taken

blocks.note: the Picts were an ancient people of northern Scotland

annotation.surface: An account of an old man from the north who is always eating curry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Northerner' suggests someone from northern England; the Picts were early inhabitants of Scotland.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: an account so vivid it creates an image, as when a writer paints one in words.

entries.clue: Ray’s maybe aloof (6)

indicatorNotes.maybe: 'maybe' flags that a ray is only one example of the class meant

annotation.surface: A remark that someone called Ray might be standoffish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ray' reads as a man's name; he is a flatfish, and the possessive turns him into 'of fish', run together.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: short for standoffish, cool and distant in manner.

entries.clue: Sorry if this is crude way to make showman be shown? (6,2,6)

annotation.definition2: way to make showman be shown?

blocks.note: said as an apology for swearing

blocks.clueFragment: way to make showman be shown
blocks.note: 'my' in French is MA; excuse (let off) MA from SHOWMAN and you get SHOWN

annotation.surface: An apology for bad language, plus an odd riddle about a showman.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is the trick: read the phrase literally, as 'leave out MA', and SHOWMAN becomes SHOWN.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom plus a literal reading: the stock apology for swearing, and an instruction to drop the French word for my.

entries.clue: One piece of information [is] all I have uncovered (4)

indicatorNotes.uncovered: uncovering takes off the cover, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: ESTATE (all I own) without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A confession that a single fact is all one has revealed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'All I have' is your estate, everything you own, and 'uncovered' strips its outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal abbreviation: short for statistic, a single datum.

entries.clue: Casual trade in island, American island (5)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the first piece inside the letter that follows

blocks.note: biz is informal for business, as in showbiz

annotation.surface: A description of informal commerce on an island owned by an American.
annotation.walkthrough: The second 'island' is the definition; the first is only I.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one of the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean, off Spain.

entries.clue: Aptly-placed lawyer[’s] battleground (9)

blocks.note: a lawyer is aptly placed in court

annotation.surface: A lawyer is in the right spot for a courtroom battle.
annotation.walkthrough: Ask where a lawyer is aptly placed and the answer is the second half.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the field in northern France where Henry V won his 1415 battle.

entries.clue: Short head[’s] feature of mouse? (7)

blocks.note: shy of = short of, as in two votes shy

annotation.surface: A horse beaten by a short head, or a note on a mouse's small head.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short head' sounds like a racing margin. The question mark flags the mouse: a mousy person is timid.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative sense of mouse: a timid, retiring person, whose defining trait is bashfulness.

entries.clue: Maximally in pain after irrational hour boomeranging (7)

indicatorNotes.boomeranging: a boomerang comes back, so the letters are read backwards
indicatorNotes.after: 'after' sends 'pain' behind the reversed piece in the answer

blocks.note: a pain is a pest, a nuisance

annotation.surface: At an absurd hour of pain returning, someone is at their very limit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' is the fashion sense, and 'maximally' makes it a superlative.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang superlative: most fashionable, where 'in' means in vogue.
